Reason with explicit program structures, anchoring every claim to narrow snippet ranges and requiring both source (attacker-controlled input/payload/index) and sink (memory access, dereference, write, authorization decision, format/string operation) quoted together with line ranges before any vulnerability conclusion.

Step 1: identify all attacker-controlled sources (arguments, parsed fields, payload indices, parsed lengths, user values, payload.data[0], network/file payload, derived pointers from untrusted counts). Quote each source snippet (≤3 lines, exact start/end with line numbers). Step 2: for each derived pointer/assignment (ptr = obj->field, idx = parsed_length, rka = authkey->payload.data[0], derived index from unvalidated count, array-derived pointer), quote both assignment line(s) and sink usage line(s) together in one paired snippet with both line ranges; state explicitly if assignment is unvalidated even when parent pointer is checked. Never rely on a single full-function range for source-to-sink. Prioritize derived-pointer assignment validation: if pointer validity at sink is never quoted, reduce confidence and state ambiguity. Step 3: at each transition verify validation shown with quoted snippet; identify missing intermediate validation; confirm data-flow reaches sink unguarded. Do not claim vulnerability without both source and sink quoted as separate snippet pairs.

Branch — for each if/else, state condition and branch for attacker-controlled input. Confirm guard is BEFORE dangerous operation (check-before-use, never after). Verify missing break/return/continue allows fallthrough past guard to sink; quote guard snippet and any fallthrough path. Check operator correctness (> vs >=, off-by-one, unsigned wrap, underflow/overflow, sign-mismatch, int64-to-int8 truncation) with quoted guard snippet including line numbers. Confirm guard applies to sink's accessed object: explicitly state "mismatch: guard checks parent (X) at line G but sink dereferences derived pointer (Y) at line S" when objects differ; include exact guard line and sink line as separate snippet pairs. For authorization/auth branches, confirm success/failure assignment cannot be unconditionally overwritten; quote both assignment and overwrite lines together.

Loop — for each for/while, state bound (constant, parsed length, packet size, user value, array length from untrusted input). Quote index derivation + array/structure access together (≤3 lines including the index expression and the access/write line). Confirm index/offset/count derived from untrusted input; verify bounds check occurs BEFORE array access/write with quoted snippet pair (check line + access line); confirm guard applies to derived pointer if loop writes through derived pointer, not only parent array/index. Verify termination (break/return/continue) exits dangerous path; quote termination snippet. Verify loop bounds against array/structure sizes explicitly with quoted snippet pairs.

Evidence anchoring mandatory before any vulnerability conclusion: quote snippet at dangerous operation (≤3 lines with start/end line numbers) and input-to-sink separately; for derived pointers include assignment + sink pair with both ranges; for loop access quote index derivation + access together; state whether guard applies to attacker-controlled path; state mismatch explicitly with both line numbers; include exact dereference/assignment/write lines; prefer narrow ranges (≤3 lines) for high confidence, wider ranges only when unavoidable — state "inference: snippet spans >3 lines" and reduce confidence. Verification rules enforcing conservative verdict (addressing observed over-labeling/precision failure): only claim vulnerability when both source and sink visible as quoted pairs, unguarded or guard misplaced/applying to wrong object, with specific line ranges; base reasoning only on given code; follow actual control flow; when guard checks parent but sink uses derived pointer, state mismatch explicitly and treat derived pointer path as unguarded rather than claiming vulnerability solely on parent check; if ambiguous (snippet >3 lines, guard object differs from sink, missing source/sink pair, full-function range used) prefer false over true and reduce confidence; set confidence proportional to evidence specificity — narrow range + snippet at both source and sink + correct guard-check = high; inference/full-range/guard-mismatch = moderate; missing source or missing sink = low/false; emphasize absence of quoted derived-pointer validity check at sink is a limitation, not evidence of vulnerability.
